input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 contains only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and security/service-failure (9.3) termination rights, plus the 9.5 savings provision; there is no Section 9.4 and no termination-for-convenience right for Customer anywhere in the Agreement. The term is three years and Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory, so no usable clause exists at either level. We insert a new Section 9.4 at the preferred position: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and no Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term. Vendor has no convenience right today, so nothing needs deleting; the take-or-pay volume commitment and its amount are left intact.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund on a pro-rata basis any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs a three-year term with no Customer right to exit without cause, so we have added Section 9.4 giving Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and barring any Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 9.4: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term

mappings.element: No more than 30 days' written notice.
No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
